articles.title: 14 states agree to raise judicial officers' retirement age to 62 yrs: SC
articles.summary:
The Supreme Court on Monday expressed satisfaction that as many as 14 states have agreed to raise the retirement age of district judicial officers from 60 to 62 years and refused to list for urgent hearing the separate pleas of judges who are on the verge of retiring or have just retired.
"This pertains to the persuasive jurisdiction of this court. The issue is between the Supreme Court and the states," a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said while declining to list individual pleas of judges who have to demit office after reaching the age of 60 years.
The CJI said that so far 14 states have agreed to raise the retirement age to 62 years and "we are hopeful that others will also follow." The bench said though it has listed the petition for hearing, it did not approve the moving of individual pleas by judicial officers.
Senior advocate Ranjit Kumar mentioned the plea for listing saying that judicial officers are retiring every day.

articles.summary: Michigan: US President Donald Trump, offering an early glimpse into the Republican Party's political future, named JD Vance and Marco Rubio among the prominent figures who could run for the White House in 2028, boasting that the GOP possesses a "great bench" compared to the Democrats.In an interview with FOX 2's Roop Raj ahead of Michigan rally, when asked directly about who might launch a presidential bid in 2028, Trump stated that while it is premature to name an outright front-runner, the party has no shortage of strong candidates."I could tell you who I think, but it's a little bit early," Trump said."We have great names - you have JD Vance, Marco Rubio, and many others. We have a great bench; they (Democrats) have no bench," Trump said.Earlier while leaving for Michigan rally, Trump while interacting with the media, also touched upon geopolitical and energy challenges stemming from the Russia-Ukraine war, reiterating that Washington would not allow global energy security to be compromised by the ongoing conflict."We're not going to be hostage with the oil industry over something that, frankly, should've never started," Trump asserted, reiterating his stance that the war was preventable.Meanwhile, the November 3 midterm elections are shaping up as a crucial contest for control of both chambers of Congress. The outcome will have significant implications for Trump's legislative agenda and the balance of political power in Washington.United States midterm elections are nationwide votes held every four years at the exact midpoint of a president's term. Acting as a major political temperature check for the country, these elections determine control of the federal government by putting all 435 seats in the House of Representatives and about one-third of the Senate up for grabs.The political contest comes amid broader challenges for the administration, including economic concerns and declining approval ratings. The Wall Street Journal reported in September that Trump's approval rating had fallen to 37 per cent in its polling, a low for a president heading into midterm elections in the publication's polling history dating back to 1990.

articles.title: PM pitches 'vocal for local' ahead of Diwali
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday delivered his 'Mann ki Baat' speech, marking 12 years of the initiative. He pitched the 'Vocal for Local' initiative ahead of the upcoming Diwali festival, saying Indians have started giving significance to  indigenous goods during festivals.He highlighted that the initiative has served as an opportunity to celebrate the hard work, courage, commitment, dedication and spirit of service of the common man of our country.Addressing the 139th Episode of Mann Ki Baat, PM Modi said, "12 years ago, on the auspicious occasion of Vijayadashami, we began 'Mann Ki Baat'. Since then, our journey has continued uninterrupted. All of you have been both fellow travellers and guides on this journey. For me, 'Mann Ki Baat' has been a wonderful opportunity to celebrate the hard work, courage, commitment, dedication and spirit of service of the common man of our country."Highlighting India's centuries-old tradition of pilgrimages, he said 'Mann Ki Baat' is not less than a pilgrimage, it is a journey to closely understand the efforts of people of the country and to pay tribute to their contributions.
